# Hermes Agent: New User FAQ & Onboarding Guide

### Installation & Environments

**Q: Which operating systems are supported natively?**
- **Linux & macOS:** Fully supported via the standard installer (`curl | bash`).
- **Windows:** Tier 1 native support via PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`) without requiring WSL2. *Note:* The web dashboard's embedded terminal `/chat` tab requires a POSIX PTY, so WSL2 is recommended if you need that specific embedded pane.
- **Docker / NAS:** Multi-arch images (`linux/amd64`, `linux/arm64`) run on Apple Silicon, Raspberry Pi, and NAS setups (UGOS, Synology, unRAID). Set `PUID` and `PGID` (or `HERMES_UID`/`HERMES_GID`) environment variables to avoid NAS bind-mount file permission errors on `/opt/data/config.yaml`.
- **Termux:** Native installation works automatically via `install.sh` (`.[termux-all]`).

**Q: Is there a Web UI?**
Yes. Run `hermes dashboard` to launch the local web UI at `http://127.0.0.1:9119`, which includes an embedded browser chat terminal.

---

### Model & Provider Configuration

**Q: Why is my local model (Ollama) slow or unresponsive?**
Hermes sends its full tool schema (~45+ tools) with every turn. Small models (4B–9B) struggle with this token overhead. To optimize:
1. Disable unnecessary tools via `hermes tools`.
2. Use faster quantization or upgrade to a 32B+ model for tool-heavy workflows.
3. Set `terminal.backend: local` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

**Q: Why does Hermes ignore my local `base_url` and send traffic elsewhere?**
When `provider: auto` is set, Hermes scans environment variables. If an API key like `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is present, it routes to that cloud service. To force local routing, set `provider: custom` with your explicit `base_url` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml`.

**Q: How do I configure specific providers?**
- **Ollama Cloud:** Use provider `ollama-cloud` with base endpoint `https://ollama.com/v1`.
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` or set `provider: azure-foundry` with `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL`.
- **Google Gemini:** Legacy CLI OAuth is deprecated. Use Google AI Studio API keys (`GEMINI_API_KEY` / `GOOGLE_API_KEY`) or Vertex AI.
- **Claude Pro/Max vs API:** Using Claude API keys bills at standard API token rates. Subscription allowances require Claude OAuth authentication.
- **Vision for Custom/Ollama Models:** Enable native image processing by adding `supports_vision: true` to your custom model config.

**Q: Can Hermes automatically route simple turns to cheaper models?**
No. Hermes intentionally maintains session model consistency. Automatic tier routing (`smart_model_routing`) is not supported. Configure subagent models via `delegation.provider` / `delegation.model` in `config.yaml`, or switch models manually in chat with `/model <name>`.

---

### Gateways & Messaging Platforms

**Q: How do I configure messaging platforms like Telegram or Discord?**
Run `hermes gateway setup` to launch the interactive platform setup wizard for Discord, Telegram, Slack, etc.

**Q: Why do I get "Unauthorized user" errors on Telegram or Discord?**
- `allowed_chats` only controls group-chat visibility, not direct message (DM) authorization.
- Authorize your DM account by setting `allow_from: "<USER_ID>"` under the platform section in `config.yaml`, approve via DM pairing code using `hermes pairing approve <platform> <CODE>`, or set `allow_all: true`.

**Q: Can gateways handle files, media, and multi-user setups?**
- **Files & Media:** Gateways (Discord, Telegram, Matrix, Email, DingTalk) support bidirectional attachments (e.g., uploading scripts, receiving Markdown images, and routing MCP tool image outputs via `MEDIA:<path>`).
- **Personas & Profiles:** Define `channel_prompts` in your gateway config for channel-specific system prompts. Use multi-profile gateways to run isolated user accounts across different channels.

---

### Memory, Persona, & Plugins

**Q: What is the difference between SOUL.md, USER.md, and MEMORY.md?**
- `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`: Agent persona, identity, and behavioral instructions.
- `~/.hermes/USER.md`: Stores persistent profile details and user preferences (`target="user"`).
- `~/.hermes/MEMORY.md`: Long-term episodic and factual agent memory.

**Q: How do I add custom tools, memory backends, or observability?**
- **Custom Tools & Memory:** In-tree additions are closed. Create standalone plugins in `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <plugin-name>`.
- **Observability:** Enable Langfuse tracing for tool inputs, outputs, and call chains with `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`.
- **Skill Usage:** Track executed skills and statistics via `hermes insights` or `/insights`.

---

### Sessions & Autonomous Execution

**Q: What should I do if the agent hits a turn limit on complex tasks?**
- Increase the turn limit in `config.yaml` (`agent.max_turns`, default 90) or per chat with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`.
- For autonomous tasks spanning across sessions, use `/goal <description>`. If paused, resume with `/goal resume`.
- Interrupted or crashed sessions are preserved as `resume_pending`; restore your transcript using `/resume`.
